_comment: Bundled default model prices for apo. Loaded idempotently on startup; this file is the SOLE source of truth for __global__ models. Per-project overrides come via the API (ticket 10). Units: USD per 1M tokens, human-readable (e.g. 2.50 = $2.50/1M); converted to micro-USD-per-million ints at load (ticket 02 #3). Pricing keys are the canonical UsageKeys (ticket 01): input, cache_read, cache_write_5m, cache_write_1h, output, reasoning. Tier conditions use ticket 05's {keys,operator,threshold} shape; the large-context tier sums input+cache_read (cached tokens occupy the context window). updated_at is pinned from JSON (NOT now()) and used for per-model exact-equality idempotency. Maintenance: see ticket 08 — review cadence is on-demand, ownership is 'whoever ships a release'.

_format.match_pattern: anchored regex; matched via re.fullmatch(pattern, name, re.IGNORECASE)
_format.prices: USD per 1M tokens; canonical usage keys: input, cache_read, cache_write_5m, cache_write_1h, output, reasoning
_format.last_reviewed: YYYY-MM; maintainer-facing staleness signal (JSON-only, never written to DB)
_format.updated_at: ISO datetime; pinned from JSON for per-model idempotency; bump to force a re-write

models._doc: Issue #102: Opus 4.6+ cut per-dimension pricing 3x vs Opus 4.5 ($5/$25 per MTok, not $15/$75). Pattern allows a date suffix (e.g. claude-opus-4-6-20260701). The earlier 'reuse the 4.5 rates' heuristic inflated every Opus 4.6/5 run by exactly 3x.
Issue #102: Opus 5 uses the same reduced rates as 4.6 ($5/$25 per MTok), not the legacy 4.5 rates. Pattern allows a date suffix.
Cache-tiered model (golden shape #3, ticket 13 §5): exercises the cache_read / cache_write_5m / cache_write_1h distinct priced dimensions.
$1/$5 per MTok. Pattern allows a date suffix — the canonical id is dated (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001). Distinct from the Claude 3.5 Haiku entry below, which is a different model at $0.80/$4.
$3/$15 per MTok. Pattern allows a date suffix.
Introductory rates through 2026-08-31: $2/$10 per MTok. Cache dimensions use Anthropic's standard multipliers of 0.1x read, 1.25x 5-minute write, and 2x 1-hour write.
Standard rates from 2026-09-01: $3/$15 per MTok.
Same reduced rates as Opus 4.6 and Opus 5 ($5/$25 per MTok).

cache_write_5m equals the input rate: this provider charges no write premium, but the tokens that populate a cache are billed as input on the call that writes them. Callers that report usage in Anthropic buckets (input_cache_creation) land on cache_write_5m for every provider, so an absent price here silently bills those tokens at zero.

Issue #76 priced this by assumption ('mirrors the 2.5-flash-lite rates') — the 2026-08-14 audit in #146's follow-up found the 3.x family above 2.5 rates. Corrected to the published rates ($0.25/$1.50 per MTok, cache read $0.025, explicit cache write $0.0833333), identical on OpenRouter and Google's direct Standard tier, so routed and direct calls bill the same. Google charges 2x for audio input ($0.50) — the text rate is used here. Pattern covers the -preview suffix the rotation actually uses. Verified 2026-08-14.

Issue #76 priced this by assumption ('Flash tier mirrors the 2.5-flash rates') — the 2026-08-14 audit in #146's follow-up found the 3.x flash family sits far above 2.5 rates. Corrected to live OpenRouter rates, which is what the routed (google/-prefixed) calls bill at: $0.75/$3.75 per MTok, cache read $0.075, explicit cache write $0.0416667. For reference Google's direct Standard tier is $1.50/$7.50/cache $0.15 (+ $1/MTok/h storage) and Batch is $0.75/$3.75 — OpenRouter's listing equals the Batch tier. Flash models are priced flat by Google: no long-context tier to model. Verified 2026-08-14.

Rates corrected 2026-09-04: this row carried $0.375/$1.875 (cache read $0.0375, write $0.0208333), which is OpenRouter's FLEX tier. A default request lands on the STANDARD tier, so 3.7 runs metered 2x low. Re-probed against openrouter.ai/api/v1/models/google/gemini-3.7-flash/endpoints (tag google-ai-studio) and ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing: $0.75/$3.75 per MTok, cache read $0.075, explicit cache write $0.0416667 — identical to the 3.6 and 3.8 rows, because Google prices the whole 3.x Flash family at one flat rate. Flash has NO long-context tier (that is Pro), so the earlier 'beyond-200k not verified' caveat did not apply either. These are introductory rates that double on 2027-01-01 across the family.

Gemini 3.8 Flash, released 2026-09-02. Rates are Google's Standard tier per ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing (verified 2026-09-03), which OpenRouter's endpoints API agrees with for the tier a default request lands on: $0.75/$3.75 per MTok, cache read $0.075, explicit cache write $0.0416667 (cheaper than input rather than equal to it, same as the 3.6 entry). INTRODUCTORY rates: Google holds them through 2026-12-31 and doubles them to $1.50/$7.50 (cache read $0.15) on 2027-01-01, which is the `discount: 0.5` OpenRouter reports on every 3.8 endpoint. Bump this row before that date, or add a dated second one with start_date 2027-01-01, or every 3.8 run reads 2x low. Flash models are priced flat by Google: no long-context tier to model. Note the 3.7 entry above carries the flex tier's rates and so under-charges 2x against the Standard tier used here.

OpenRouter lists flash at $1.50/$9.00 per MTok (cache read $0.15, explicit cache write $0.0833333). Anchored exactly so it cannot swallow the 5x-cheaper flash-lite sibling. Flash models are priced flat by Google: no long-context tier to model.

2026-08-30 refresh: OpenRouter lists flash-lite at $0.30/$2.50 per MTok (cache read $0.03, explicit cache write $0.0833333 — the same write rate as flash, so writes are relatively costlier here). The pattern tolerates a -preview rotation suffix like the 3.1 flash-lite entry. Flash models are priced flat by Google: no long-context tier to model.

2026-08-30 refresh: grok-4.5 was arriving unpriced (xAI via OpenRouter, provider stays 'generic' — matching keys on pattern only). Anchored to the exact id so a grok-4.5-fast does not silently inherit these prices.
